metaTitle: Sand Fleas: What They Are and Do They Bite?
metaDescription: Sand fleas on US beaches are harmless beach hoppers and mole crabs. See photos, the beach bugs that do bite, the chigoe flea, and how to treat bites.
h1: Sand Fleas: What They Are, Do They Bite, and What Is Biting You at the Beach
dek: Real photos of the beach hoppers and mole crabs called sand fleas and of the beach bugs that really bite, plus the chigoe flea that burrows into feet in the tropics, what the bites look like and when to see a doctor.
excerpt: What sand fleas are, whether they bite, which beach bugs do, the tropical chigoe flea, and how to treat and avoid bites, with real photos.

quickAnswer.lead: **On US beaches, the animals called sand fleas are crustaceans: beach hoppers, small jumping scavengers of washed-up seaweed that an entomology textbook calls harmless, and mole crabs, the surf-zone fishing bait that cannot bite or pinch.** Bites blamed on them can come from biting midges, stable flies or fleas; the sand flea that burrows into skin, the chigoe flea, lives in the tropics and subtropics.
bullets: Beach hoppers are amphipods related to crabs and shrimp, called sand fleas for their long jumps, says the [National Park Service](https://www.nps.gov/glba/learn/nature/snails-limpets-chitons.htm); the California beach hopper grows to about 1.1 inches ([Walla Walla University](https://inverts.wallawalla.edu/Arthropoda/Crustacea/Malacostraca/Eumalacostraca/Peracarida/Amphipoda/Gammaridea/Talitridae/Megalorchestia_californiana.html)).

Gulf Coast mole crabs are about 1/2 inch to 1 inch long and clawless, so they cannot bite or pinch, says [UF/IFAS Extension](https://blogs.ifas.ufl.edu/escambiaco/2021/09/01/weekly-what-is-it-sand-fleas-mole-crabs/).

Biting midges, also called no-see-ums or sand flies, are usually 1/25 to 1/12 inch long and are often persistent pests of US beachgoers, according to [the University of Florida](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN626).
Stable flies lay eggs in seaweed washed up on beaches, and large outbreaks on the Gulf Coast have driven beachgoers away ([UF/IFAS](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IG081)).
The mated female chigoe flea burrows into skin, usually between the toes or under the toenails, and swells up to about 3/8 inch (1 cm), [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/dpdx/tungiasis/index.html) says.

body.text: What are sand fleas?

Sand flea is a nickname for several unrelated animals, not one species. On US beaches the name is given to two small crustaceans, beach hoppers and mole crabs; in the tropics it also means the chigoe flea, a true flea that burrows into skin. [Cleveland Clinic's guide to sand flea bites](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/24458-sand-flea-bites) notes that the most common and least dangerous sand fleas are crustaceans, kin to crabs and lobsters, also known as sand hoppers, beach fleas or beach hoppers.

body.alt: Pale tan beach hopper on gray sand, a segmented crustacean with a round black eye, several pairs of thin legs and long orange-red antennae
body.caption: A California beach hopper, *Megalorchestia californiana*, on sand. Walla Walla University notes the species' pinkish-orange to red antennae and says it hides in a burrow by day and feeds on decaying seaweed at night.

body.text: Beach hoppers are amphipods, relatives of crabs and shrimp, and the [National Park Service](https://www.nps.gov/glba/learn/nature/snails-limpets-chitons.htm) says they are often called sand fleas because they can jump impressive distances. Mole crabs are the sand fleas that surf anglers dig out of the wash of the waves.

The names overlap. [CDC's parasitology page on tungiasis](https://www.cdc.gov/dpdx/tungiasis/index.html) lists jigger among the chigoe flea's other names, and Walter Ebeling's *Urban Entomology*, a 1975 textbook hosted by [UC Riverside's entomology department](https://entomology.ucr.edu/ebeling_ch9_3), says it has been called a chigger as well, though the true chigger is the larva of a mite.
What do beach hoppers look like, and where do they live?

Beach hoppers vary by species. The one in the photo above, the California beach hopper, has an ivory, gray-white or gray-green body, round black eyes and pinkish-orange to reddish antennae, and grows to about 1.1 inches (2.8 cm), according to [Walla Walla University's invertebrate guide](https://inverts.wallawalla.edu/Arthropoda/Crustacea/Malacostraca/Eumalacostraca/Peracarida/Amphipoda/Gammaridea/Talitridae/Megalorchestia_californiana.html). It lives on Pacific beaches from southern California north into Canada.

Look for them where the high tide leaves its debris. Walla Walla says the California beach hopper lives high on wide, fine-sand beaches, usually near decaying seaweed. It hides by day in burrows up to about 12 inches (30 cm) deep, comes out at night to feed on the seaweed and often moves down toward the waterline to eat.

On the Atlantic coast, the [National Park Service at Cape Cod](https://www.nps.gov/caco/learn/nature/beaches.htm) describes wrack, the mix of seaweed and salt marsh plants that high tides leave on the beach, as home to numerous invertebrates, with amphipods among the animals that shred it.

body.needed: Beach hoppers under a clump of washed-up seaweed at the high-tide line on a US Atlantic or Gulf Coast beach, with a coin or ruler for scale, identified by an expert or as a research-grade observation; public domain or CC0

body.text: Do sand fleas bite?

The crustaceans called sand fleas do not feed on blood: beach hoppers eat decaying seaweed, and mole crabs strain plankton and debris from the water. Both are described as harmless. Ebeling's text says the small amphipods called sand fleas that live under beached seaweed get blamed for bites but are entirely harmless, and [UF/IFAS Extension in Escambia County, Florida](https://blogs.ifas.ufl.edu/escambiaco/2021/09/01/weekly-what-is-it-sand-fleas-mole-crabs/) says mole crabs are clawless and cannot bite or pinch.

One medical source is less categorical: Cleveland Clinic says these crustaceans might cause red, itchy bumps that usually go away in a few days. If you were bitten on the sand, consider the insects that share the beach. Ebeling names two: fleas, which may turn up on beaches near homes, and stable flies, often found in piles of seaweed.
The chigoe flea, covered below, is the exception: its mated females burrow into the skin.
What are the mole crabs anglers call sand fleas?

Mole crabs are small, oval crustaceans that live in the swash zone, the wet sand where waves break and run up the beach. The [Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission](https://myfwc.com/wildlifehabitats/profiles/invertebrates/mole-crab/) describes the Atlantic mole crab, *Emerita talpoida*, as light brownish gray and up to 2 inches long, with five pairs of legs, no claws on the first pair and two feathery antennae for filtering plankton and debris from the water. It digs into the sand tail first.

body.alt: Atlantic mole crab, a smooth, oval, pinkish-brown crustacean with pale feathery appendages tucked beneath it, resting on a white surface
body.caption: An Atlantic mole crab, *Emerita talpoida*, from Assateague Island National Seashore in Maryland. Mole crabs are clawless and cannot bite or pinch, UF/IFAS Extension says.

body.text: UF/IFAS Extension puts the sand fleas of Florida's Gulf Coast at about 1/2 inch to 1 inch long, with rounded white or gray shells. They are the sand fleas of surf fishing: most local fishermen consider them the perfect bait for pompano, UF/IFAS says, and collect them with a combined rake, shovel and sieve.
Which beach bugs bite?
Several insects bite on US beaches, and any of them can leave bites that get blamed on sand fleas: biting midges, stable flies, greenheads, mosquitoes and, near homes, fleas.
Biting midges (no-see-ums)

Biting midges are tiny bloodsucking flies, also called no-see-ums, sand flies or sand gnats. The [University of Florida's profile of biting midges](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN626) calls them often abundant and persistent pests of beachgoers, campers and fishers in US coastal areas. Adults are usually 1/25 to 1/12 inch long (1 to 2 mm), most with spotted wings, and in Florida several coastal species breed in marshes, swamps and mangroves. Most species bite at dusk, at night or in the morning, but in coastal areas many bite in broad daylight. [The guide to no-see-ums](/blog/no-see-ums) covers them in full, and [no-see-um bites](/blog/no-see-um-bites) shows what their bites look like.

body.alt: Tiny dark biting midge with mottled gray wings standing on pale, finely creased human skin among a few hairs
body.caption: A biting midge on human skin, in a photo from CSIRO, whose description calls biting midges a common nuisance around marine environments. UF/IFAS gives the usual length of adults as 1/25 to 1/12 inch.
body.credit: division, CSIRO, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

body.text: A [UF/IFAS fact sheet on biting flies](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IG081) adds that only the females bite, that little feeding happens in even a slight breeze, and that in Florida the midges are most abundant in summer but may bite at any time of year.
Stable flies

Stable flies, also called dog flies, look like house flies in size and color, but their large piercing mouthparts point forward from the head, and both males and females feed on blood, UF/IFAS says. Females lay eggs in places such as soiled animal bedding, compost piles and even seaweed piled on beaches, and big stable fly populations on the Gulf Coast have driven beachgoers away. In Florida they are most abundant in late fall, peaking in early January.

body.alt: Close side view of a gray, bristly stable fly with large red-brown eyes standing on pink skin, its slender black mouthparts angled down to the skin
body.caption: A stable fly feeding on a person's skin at a forest preserve in the US, as its photographer describes it. UF/IFAS says the forward-pointing piercing mouthparts tell it apart from a house fly.
body.credit: Peterwchen, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

body.text: Greenheads and other horse flies

The greenhead, *Tabanus nigrovittatus*, belongs to *Tabanus*, the horse fly genus in [UF/IFAS's profile of horse flies and deer flies](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN155). [Rutgers University entomologists](https://entomology.rutgers.edu/outreach/greenheads.html) call it an abundant summer pest along coastal marshes and suggest fly traps on beaches as well as at the marsh edge; the females bite in daylight, from late June into September, with numbers peaking in July. UF/IFAS's biting flies fact sheet says horse flies and deer flies cut the skin with large mouthparts, that the wounds can become infected and that many people are allergic to the bites. See [why horse fly and deer fly bites hurt](/blog/horse-fly-and-deer-fly-bite-treatment), [the greenhead fly guide](/blog/greenhead-flies) and [how to tell a deer fly from a horse fly](/blog/deer-fly-vs-horse-fly).

body.alt: Greenhead fly seen from above on white fabric, a stout brown fly with large iridescent green eyes and clear wings with amber veins
body.caption: A greenhead, the salt marsh horse fly *Tabanus nigrovittatus*, on Sapelo Island, Georgia. Rutgers University says the females bite by day and that greenhead numbers peak in July.
body.credit: Judy Gallagher, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

body.text: Mosquitoes and fleas

The black salt marsh mosquito breeds in coastal salt marshes but has a long flight range, says [the University of Florida's profile of the species](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN1035), which calls it very common in eastern coastal areas of the Americas and notorious for emerging in large numbers after rain and flooding and for biting aggressively, mostly at night. [The guide to keeping mosquitoes away](/blog/how-to-keep-mosquitoes-away) covers repellents and timing.

Fleas can turn up on beaches too, particularly near homes, Ebeling says. [Fleas on people](/blog/fleas-on-humans) covers how fleas end up biting humans, and [what flea bites look like](/blog/flea-bites) covers the bites.
What is the chigoe flea, the sand flea that burrows into skin?

The chigoe flea, *Tunga penetrans*, is a true flea and the cause of tungiasis. [CDC's tungiasis page](https://www.cdc.gov/dpdx/tungiasis/index.html) says it lives in tropical and subtropical regions, including Mexico to South America, the West Indies and Africa, usually in sandy places such as beaches, stables and farms, and that people pick it up by walking barefoot there. Males and females both feed on blood, but only mated females burrow into the skin, leaving just the rear end exposed. Each keeps feeding, swells up to about 3/8 inch (1 cm), sheds about 100 eggs over two weeks, then dies and is sloughed off with the skin.

Before it burrows it is tiny: Ebeling describes a reddish-brown flea about 1/25 inch (1 mm) long. [Cleveland Clinic's tungiasis page](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/24162-tungiasis) says the fleas that cause tungiasis don't live in the United States, and Ebeling wrote that the chigoe was not definitely known to have become established here.

Cleveland Clinic says you probably won't notice the flea entering your skin; you may then see a white circle like a ring or halo with a black dot in the center, most often on the soles, between the toes, at the heel or along the outside of the foot. CDC says lesions are usually between the toes or under the toenails, that itching and irritation usually begin as the female becomes fully developed, that multiple lesions on the feet can make walking hard, and that secondary bacterial infections, including tetanus and gangrene, are not uncommon.

body.needed: A chigoe flea lesion (tungiasis) on a foot: a white ring with a dark center between the toes or at the heel, from CDC PHIL or another public domain medical source, shown small and low on the page

body.text: Are sand fleas the same as sand flies?

No. The sand fleas of US beaches are crustaceans, and sand flies are insects. UF/IFAS lists sand fly, along with no-see-um and sand gnat, among the common names of biting midges, the coastal biters described above.

The sand flies that spread leishmaniasis, a parasitic disease found in parts of about 90 countries, usually tropical or subtropical, are different insects. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/leishmaniasis/about/index.html) says they are silent, about a quarter the size of mosquitoes and usually most active from dusk to dawn, and that people occasionally catch the skin form in the US, especially in Texas.
What do sand flea bites look like?

Usually like small red bumps on the ankles and feet. Cleveland Clinic describes sand flea bites as small, red, raised bumps, sometimes in clusters, that tend to occur on the ankles and feet and usually clear up in a few days. Many insect bites look alike, so where and when you were bitten matters.

Biting midge bites generally cause a local stinging or burning feeling with a defined red area around each bite, UF/IFAS says; the discomfort usually lasts minutes to hours, though people who are hypersensitive may itch for two to three days.

body.alt: Backs of a man's lower legs above rolled-down white socks, with several small reddish bite marks around both ankles
body.caption: Biting midge bites on a man's ankles, where he had rolled down his socks, in a CDC photograph from a case in Costa Rica. UF/IFAS describes a stinging or burning feeling and a red area around each midge bite.
body.credit: CDC/ Margaret Parsons; photo: C. L. Hogue (CDC Public Health Image Library, phil.cdc.gov)

body.text: A chigoe flea leaves the white ring with a black dot described above. To compare your bites with others by pattern, place and timing, use the [bug bite identification chart](/learn/bug-bites), or answer six questions in the [bug bite identifier](/tools/bug-bite-identifier).

body.text: What should you do about a sand flea bite?
For an ordinary itchy bite, [MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000033.htm), the National Library of Medicine's consumer health site, gives these steps:

items: Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and water.
Hold ice wrapped in a washcloth on it for 10 minutes, take it off for 10 minutes, and repeat.
If needed, take an antihistamine or use a cream that reduces itching. Cleveland Clinic names calamine lotion as one such cream and says to use an antihistamine as a cream or by mouth, not both.
Over the next several days, watch for signs of infection, such as increasing redness, swelling or pain.

body.text: Never dig out a chigoe flea yourself. Cleveland Clinic says a burrowed sand flea should be removed only by a healthcare provider, with sterilized tools such as forceps or a needle, or other proven methods.

body.title: When to get medical care
body.text: Call 911 for signs of a severe allergic reaction, which MedlinePlus says can follow insect bites as well as stings: trouble breathing, swelling of the face or mouth, throat tightness or trouble swallowing, feeling weak, or turning blue. Cleveland Clinic says open sores, ulcers or signs of infection need immediate medical attention. After time in a place with chigoe fleas, call a provider about a white lesion on the foot, ankle or elsewhere, or an itchy or painful rash. See one for any rash or irritation that lasts more than a few days.
How can you avoid bites at the beach?
Match the defense to the biter:

items: **Use a repellent made for biting flies.** The [CDC Yellow Book](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/environmental-hazards-risks/mosquitoes-ticks-and-other-arthropods.html) says EPA-registered repellents labeled for flies, biting flies and no-see-ums repel biting midges, and its general repellent section lists DEET, picaridin, IR3535, oil of lemon eucalyptus or PMD, and 2-undecanone as active ingredients that typically give reasonably long-lasting protection. UF/IFAS says DEET-based repellents are the main ones used against biting midges, and that most repellents work less well on biting flies than on mosquitoes, so they need reapplying more often; follow the label. [Whether DEET is safe](/blog/is-deet-safe) has its own guide.

**Choose your hours, and a breeze.** UF/IFAS says biting midges are usually most active around sunrise and sunset and feed little in even a slight breeze, while stable flies, deer flies and horse flies are usually most active during the day.

**Cover up.** Long sleeves and long pants protect arms and legs from biting flies, UF/IFAS says. CDC adds long socks, since flea bites often land on the lower legs and feet, and closed shoes instead of sandals.

**Keep shoes on in the tropics.** People pick up chigoe fleas walking barefoot in tropical and subtropical regions, CDC says, and Cleveland Clinic advises closed-toe shoes, socks that cover the ankles and long pants where they occur.
**Use finer screens at a beach rental.** CDC says the insect screens commonly used on windows do not stop biting midges and recommends 20x20 mesh.

body.title: Save the evidence
body.text: Catch a biter in a clear jar or photograph it beside a ruler marked in inches, and note where you were, the time of day and whether a breeze was blowing. Your state's cooperative extension office can use those details to help identify it.

faqs.question: Do sand fleas carry diseases?
faqs.answer: None of the sources on this page links the beach hoppers or mole crabs called sand fleas to any disease. The health risks attached to the name come from other animals. The chigoe flea of the tropics causes tungiasis, and CDC says secondary bacterial infections, including tetanus and gangrene, are not uncommon with it. UF/IFAS says some biting midges spread Oropouche virus in South America and the Caribbean, and CDC says sand flies spread leishmaniasis in parts of about 90 countries.

faqs.question: How long do sand flea bites last?
faqs.answer: It depends on what bit you. Cleveland Clinic says common sand flea bites usually clear up in a few days. UF/IFAS says the stinging or burning from a biting midge bite usually lasts minutes to hours, though people who are hypersensitive may itch for two to three days. A chigoe flea is different because it stays in the skin: Cleveland Clinic says it can live there for up to six weeks. See a healthcare provider for any rash or irritation that does not go away in a few days, Cleveland Clinic advises.

faqs.question: Can sand flea bites get infected?
faqs.answer: Yes. MedlinePlus advises watching an insect bite over the next several days for signs of infection, such as increasing redness, swelling or pain, and Cleveland Clinic says open sores, ulcers or signs of infection need immediate medical attention. With the chigoe flea, CDC says secondary bacterial infections, including tetanus and gangrene, are not uncommon, and Cleveland Clinic warns that only a healthcare provider using sterilized tools should remove a burrowed flea.

faqs.question: What repels sand fleas?
faqs.answer: Repellent is for the insects that bite at the beach, since the beach hoppers and mole crabs called sand fleas feed on seaweed and plankton, not blood. CDC's Yellow Book says EPA-registered repellents labeled for flies, biting flies and no-see-ums are effective against biting midges, and its general repellent section lists DEET, picaridin, IR3535, oil of lemon eucalyptus or PMD, and 2-undecanone as active ingredients that typically give reasonably long-lasting protection. UF/IFAS adds that most repellents work less well against biting flies than against mosquitoes, so they need reapplying more often; follow the label.

faqs.question: Can sand fleas come home with you?
faqs.answer: The beach hoppers and mole crabs called sand fleas are shore animals. The sources on this page describe beach hoppers in sand and washed-up seaweed high on the beach and mole crabs in the wet sand where waves break, and none describes either one living indoors. The chigoe flea of the tropics is different: Cleveland Clinic says travelers to the areas where it lives may return home carrying it. If bites start at home after a beach trip, check pets for ordinary fleas: UC Riverside's Ebeling text says the cat flea and dog flea are the most common fleas in and around homes, and CDC notes that flea bites often land on the lower legs and feet.

faqs.question: Are there sand fleas in Florida?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the beach sense of the name. UF/IFAS Extension in Escambia County describes the mole crabs that wash up in the waves on Florida beaches as sand fleas, and says most local fishermen consider them the perfect bait for pompano. Florida also has the biters blamed on sand fleas: about 50 species of Culicoides biting midges, according to UF/IFAS, and stable flies, whose outbreaks on the Gulf Coast have driven beachgoers away. The chigoe flea, which burrows into skin, does not live in the United States, Cleveland Clinic says.

faqs.question: Are sand fleas crustaceans or insects?
faqs.answer: It depends on which sand flea. The beach hoppers and mole crabs called sand fleas on US beaches are crustaceans: the National Park Service describes beach hoppers as amphipods related to crabs and shrimp, and Cleveland Clinic says the most common sand fleas are crustaceans, kin to crabs and lobsters. The chigoe flea of the tropics is an insect, a true flea whose mated females burrow into skin, according to CDC. The biting midges sometimes called sand flies are insects too.

faqs.question: What do sand fleas eat?
faqs.answer: Beach hoppers eat seaweed that washes up on the beach. Walla Walla University says the California beach hopper hides in a burrow by day and comes out at night to feed on decaying seaweed, and the National Park Service describes beach hoppers feeding on clumps of algae that wash ashore. Mole crabs filter plankton and debris from the water with their feathery antennae, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. Neither feeds on blood. The chigoe flea does: CDC says both males and females feed on their host.

faqs.question: Can you get tungiasis in the United States?
faqs.answer: Not from US beaches, as far as the sources say. Cleveland Clinic states that the types of fleas that cause tungiasis don't live in the United States, and Walter Ebeling's urban entomology text says the chigoe flea was not definitely known to have become established here. CDC says people pick it up by walking barefoot in tropical and subtropical regions, including Mexico to South America, the West Indies and Africa. After time in such a place, a white lesion on the foot is a reason to call a healthcare provider.

faqs.question: What time of day are sand fleas most active?
faqs.answer: The California beach hopper is a night animal: Walla Walla University says it hides in a burrow in the sand by day and comes out at night to feed, often moving down toward the waterline. The insects blamed for sand flea bites keep other hours. UF/IFAS says biting midges are usually most active around sunrise and sunset, though in coastal areas many bite in broad daylight; stable flies, deer flies and horse flies are usually most active during the day, and the black salt marsh mosquito feeds mainly at night.
